Use this to compute the energy participations (EPR) of a mode again from the
fields that an HFSS Eigenmode run with EPR has already saved, without solving
again: to get the participations of the final fields rather than of the
adaptive passes, or to choose where a surface's field is read. AEDT opens a
copy of the returned project, reads the saved fields, evaluates the EPR
expressions and writes `results/epr/epr-result.json`, which
[Change loss assumptions](offline-loss.qmd) then takes. This repository holds
no recorded result of it.

You need:

- the complete returned run folder of an HFSS Eigenmode run that requested
  EPR, as in [Flip-chip Xmon with AEDT](xmon/aedt.qmd), read once as in
  [Convergence and reports](convergence-and-reports.qmd#aedt-read-the-sealed-family-evidence);
  an `.aedt` project file alone is not enough;
- AEDT 2023.2 or 2024.2 with PyAEDT 1.3.0 and a licence, on the computer that
  runs the analysis.

## Recover the exact prepared model {#recover-the-exact-prepared-model}

Read the model and the request from the returned run folder itself, not by
building the layout again: a PDK that changed since would give a different
model.

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import parse_aedt_spec, resolve_saved_solution

returned_run_dir = Path(".artifacts/returned-aedt-epr")
spec = parse_aedt_spec(
    json.loads((returned_run_dir / "aedt_spec.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    base_dir=returned_run_dir,  # the request's SGB model is in its model/ folder
)
saved = resolve_saved_solution(returned_run_dir / "saved-solution-manifest.json")
```

Use the folder the run returned. `parse_aedt_spec` gives back the request:
its model, run controls and EPR request. `resolve_saved_solution` checks,
before AEDT opens, that every saved file listed in the run's manifest is
there and unchanged; a missing or changed file stops it. Only a run that
requested EPR saves these fields: a plain Eigenmode run has none to analyse.

## Evaluate in a new analysis folder {#evaluate-in-a-new-analysis-directory}

```python
from scgsim.aedt import analyze_epr

AEDT_VERSION = "2024.2"  # Choose explicitly: 2023.2 or 2024.2.
final_epr = analyze_epr(
    aedt_version=AEDT_VERSION,
    saved_solution=saved,
    model=spec.model,
    project_name=spec.project_name,
    design_name=spec.design_name,
    run_control=spec.run_control,
    epr_request=spec.epr_request,
    output_dir=Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-saved-field-analysis"),
)
```

`analyze_epr` copies the saved project into the new `output_dir`, opens the
copy, checks that it is the same model, design, setup and pass, and evaluates
the requested participations from the saved fields; it neither solves nor
exports fields. The returned run stays as it was. If the fields or the EPR
expressions are missing, it fails instead of falling back on the adaptive
history. `final_epr` is the result that
`.artifacts/public-xmon-saved-field-analysis/results/epr/epr-result.json`
holds.

The AEDT release is the one you choose here. If the returned run does not
record which release saved the fields, that stays unknown; the analysis runs
with the release you chose.

A surface's field can be read on its film's sheet or just beside it:
`surface_field_selectors={group: "surface"}` (the default) or
`{group: "adjacent"}`, keyed by a Surface EPR group of the request. A group
the request does not select, or another value, is an error. The choice
changes no geometry and starts no solve; the
[runtime reference](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd) describes both, and
the [`analyze_epr` reference](../reference/api/analyze-epr.qmd) every argument.

The participations of the final fields are a different result from those of
the adaptive passes: an inset margin evaluated here belongs to this result
only, not to the history. Continue with
[Change loss assumptions](offline-loss.qmd#aedt-final-fields-and-adaptive-history-stay-separate)
to apply other loss tangents to `final_epr`.
